action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is still to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is intact, and this kind of phase has historically been when spending to win new and returning users paid back best, especially among active traders. Apply it with extra care now: Bitcoin has been under its 50-day average for 19 days (about 8% below it), is down about 10% in 30 days, the mood reads fear at 29 out of 100, and price is only about 2% above its 200-day average of $73,160, so today's signal confidence is low. Keep any increase small and easy to pause, lead with trust, safety and explainer messages, speed up only once price closes back above about $81,641, and pause the increase if price closes below $73,160. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

watch: Bitcoin is now only about 2% above its 200-day average, the main line holding up the long-run uptrend, with US inflation data due on Tuesday. A close below $73,160 would put that uptrend in question, while a close back above $76,750 would ease the pressure.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run uptrend still holds, but the coming week looks soft and price is now close to the level that matters most. At about $74,845, Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 19 days, sits about 8% below it and about 11% below its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 29 (fear); Pluang reports a sharp sell-off in US tech and AI stocks forced about $1 billion of bets on a rise to close, taking Bitcoin to its lowest since August, and news is taking a little more off the week, with a five-hour outage at Upbit and a security warning from LNbits (PANews). A normal week swings about $3,881, so a close above $76,750 (top of a typical week's swing) would turn it clearly up, a close below $73,160 (the 200-day average) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy. US inflation data on Tuesday (PANews) is the near-term event to watch; a close under $73,160 is the cue for safety-first messaging.

The next month is mixed. The 90-day numbers still point up, with price about 18% higher and about 92% of those days closing above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 10%, Bitcoin funds saw about $487 million leave in a single day, and Bitcoin is moving closely with US tech stocks. Price must win back $81,641 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there room to climb further; while it stays under that average, the month keeps fading. The next Fed meeting is on 8 December, so keep bigger campaign pushes for a reclaim of the 50-day average.

The 3-6 month picture leans up at a moderate strength. Price is only about 2% above its 200-day average, which is still rising about 5% over 90 days, while Bitcoin remains about 40% below its all-time high. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,160 (the 200-day average); if that goes, $67,428 (the 200-week average) is the next floor, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. A small long-run positive is that Russia's central bank has finalized rules letting ordinary people trade crypto from 17 November (PANews); a close below the 200-day average is what would weaken this picture and be the moment to shift budget toward keeping existing users.
